releases.name: Phux Rune 0.1.36
releases.body:
**Phux Rune 0.1.36**: 6 changes since 0.1.35.

- Make phone questions readable and touchable (#2636)
- Apply defaults.clipboard-write to pane osc 52 writes (#2638)
- Drop a terminal on a pane to make it a tab of that split (#2635)
- Tabs inside a split: ⌘⇧←/→, a 2/3 badge, hidden tabs kept warm (#2628)
- Draw Kitty images, with one upload per image change (#2618)
- Clients carry slot tabs, and phux slot add|out|next|prev (#2622)

releases.name: Phux Rune 0.1.33
releases.body:
**Phux Rune 0.1.33**: long text fields stay accessible.

- Track Rune dev `0796df5f` from `bc05f817`, including both native
  accessibility adapters. On macOS, text fields above 64 KiB, or with paragraphs
  still waiting to be shaped, retain their complete value and selection
  ranges instead of exposing an absent or partial text document. Range queries
  are answered lazily; lines follow newline boundaries and have no rectangles.
- Accessibility text runs no longer copy the entire field once per line.
  Normal password masking and short-field IME display handling remain intact.
- Inherit Rune's paragraph-field highlight/reveal fixes. Terminal Find still
  searches the loaded terminal grid; this does not add Find inside ACP editors.

Known upstream limitation (`phux-eqdvh`): in the new macOS fallback, an
AppKit UTF-16 query inside an emoji's surrogate pair rounds forward to the
following character, which can also shift selection/edit boundaries.
This also affects partially shaped fields below 64 KiB.
Fully shaped normal fields keep their existing run-backed path. The finding is
tracked, with a reproduction retained; no local framework fork is included.

This does not add native iOS VoiceOver support or prove physical-device feel.
Signed phone installation is reconciled separately from desktop publication;
an unsigned device build or simulator screenshot is not phone delivery.

releases.name: Phux Rune 0.1.32
releases.body:
**Phux Rune 0.1.32** keeps window colors steady as the GPU takes over and
includes Rune's macOS accessibility crash fix.

- Translucent fills and grayscale text edges use byte-precision blend sources
  in the default window pass, reducing CPU/GPU handover drift on desktop
  and native iOS without changing layout or terminal input.
- The macOS accessibility adapter no longer races or aborts when AppKit
  answers the process's own accessibility query on a background thread.
- Tracks Rune dev `bc05f817`. All five upstream workspace patches move with
  the framework; Linux and macOS archives retain their usual verification.

Native iOS continues to qualify paired QUIC and WSS, saved-key reconnect,
UIKit editing and real OS background/foreground rendering in the simulator.
Simulator and device linking are not physical-device feel, VoiceOver or
OS keyboard/IME qualification. Scheduled ad-hoc phone installation remains
separate from this desktop release and requires valid local signing access.
